newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares eke out modest gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares eke out modest gains at close.

text.p: Local punters dominated a listless Philippine equities market on Friday, nibbling on secondliners which later led to modest gains at the close, brokers said.
The composite index nudged up 19.24 points, or 0.74 percent, to close at 2,635.64 amid a slim turnover of 1.4 billion pesos.
"The biggest factor that's affecting the market is uncertainty. There's no real commitment to go long or to go short," Raymond Garcia, vice president of Diversified Securities, said.
The foreign exchange and money markets were still edgy as speculative pressure on regional currencies persisted.
Eagle Equities president Joey Roxas said foreigners opted to stay out of the market, leaving it open to local punters.
"We saw a lot of activities in small cap issues ... Trading today was speculative in nature," Roxas added.
With Wall Street hitting new highs, Garcia said foreign players shifted their focus away from the troubled southeast Asian markets.
Gaming concern Belle Corp was the most heavily traded stock as it rose 10 centavos to close at 6.60 pesos. Blue chips such as Manila Electric B and Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co followed suit.
